title: Clinic waiting time and appointments review

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Thanks for staying after the evening clinic. I'll keep this to fifteen minutes.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: No problem, the last patient left early today.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: The waiting room situation. Arif, what are the numbers?

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: Average wait last month was seventy minutes in the morning. Afternoons are fine, around twenty.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: The mornings are mostly walk-ins. They all arrive at nine and the appointment patients get stuck behind them.

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: The booking system shows the same. Morning appointments start late almost every day.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: We can't stop walk-ins altogether, a lot of our elderly patients don't book.

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: What if walk-ins only come in a fixed window, say nine to eleven?

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: That would help the nurses plan the vitals and dressings.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: I like it. Walk-ins are seen only between 9 and 11 in the morning; the rest of the day is by appointment.

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: Emergencies are still seen any time, of course.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Yes, emergencies are always seen, that's not changing.

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: Then I'll need to retrain the front desk on how to explain this to patients.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Arif, please run that retraining for the front desk by Saturday, before the rush on Monday.

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: I'll do the retraining by Saturday, one session for both shifts.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: Also people forget their appointments. We had eleven no-shows last week.

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: The booking system can send SMS reminders. We just never turned it on.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Why not?

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: It needs the sender ID approved, and someone has to write the message text.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Let's do it. Every patient gets an SMS reminder the day before the appointment.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: Can it include the clinic phone number, for cancellations?

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: Yes, I'll add the number to the template.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Kunal, when can the reminders be running?

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: The sender ID approval takes a few days. I'll have the SMS reminders running next Monday.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: And separately, the vaccine stock audit is on 18 December, so I'll be counting fridges that week.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Thanks for the reminder, Priya, I'll keep that day light for you.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: One more idea. What if we open on Sunday mornings? Many working patients ask for it.

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: We don't have the staff. Two people already do six days.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Sunday opening would need new hiring. It's not happening now.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: Fair, I'll tell the patients who asked that it's not planned.

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: The new walk-in hours need to be visible, or patients will argue at the desk.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: We need to put up a notice about the new walk-in hours at the entrance, and at the pharmacy counter too.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: In Marathi and English, please. Many patients don't read English.

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: Not me, I have no idea how to print anything that looks nice.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Fine, we'll sort out the notice later this week.

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: The token machine is also acting up. It printed duplicate numbers twice yesterday.

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: That's a paper sensor issue, I've seen it before. I'll clean it tomorrow morning.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: The sterilizer service is overdue too, by about two weeks.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Call the service company, it can't wait.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: I called them on Tuesday, they said next week.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Push them, please. We can't run the minor procedures without it.

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: On a happier note, the feedback forms this month were mostly positive.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: What did people complain about?

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: The waiting, mostly. And the drinking water dispenser on the first floor.

segments.speaker: Kunal Mehra
segments.text: The dispenser needs a new filter, it's a small purchase.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Go ahead and buy it, no need to ask.

segments.speaker: Priya Varghese
segments.text: Will the doctors know about the walk-in window?

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: I'll tell them at Monday's morning huddle.

segments.speaker: Arif Hussain
segments.text: Good, otherwise they'll keep calling walk-ins in at noon.

segments.speaker: Sunita Kulkarni
segments.text: Thank you all. Let's go home.

decisions.fact: Walk-in patients are seen only from 9 to 11 am; other times are by appointment.
Patients get an SMS reminder the day before their appointment.

action_items.fact: Kunal turns on the SMS appointment reminders.
Arif retrains the front desk staff on the new walk-in rules.
A notice about the walk-in hours goes up at the entrance and pharmacy; nobody named.

distractors.fact: Opening on Sunday mornings was suggested and rejected.
18 December is the vaccine stock audit, not the SMS reminders' date.
